archetype.name: Dual-Threat (legs fading)
archetype.definition: A run-pass quarterback whose value has always rested on scrambling, designed runs and accurate intermediate throws, but whose rushing has thinned and whose short-area passing has broken down this year.

report.headline: Downfield arm still works; everything short and his job status don't
report.take:
Hurts has been a Dual-Threat quarterback since his rookie year. He led the position in rushing yards in 2021, and through 2024 he paired that with plus accuracy: a CPOE ranked 1st in 2024 and bad-throw rates around 13-14% every season from 2021 on. The 2026 version is a different, narrower player. He is at -2.55 CPOE (36th of 47), his bad-throw rate has climbed to 21.4% (37th of 38, up 7.1 points on last year), and his rushing is down to 21.4 yards a game. The designed runs have died: they go for 1.11 yards a carry and get stuffed 55.6% of the time.

The season splits sharply by depth. Throws of 10+ air yards are excellent: 0.878 EPA a play, an 8.7 CPOE, and six of his eight TDs. Everything under 10 air yards is a disaster at -0.352 EPA a play, and screens behind the line are worse at -0.887. Those two halves roughly cancel, which is why his passing EPA per dropback sits just below average. The short game isn't only on him. Philadelphia ranks 30th in offensive EPA and 31st in success rate, and under-center plays (-0.343 EPA, 37.5% completions) point to a play-action and quick game that isn't functioning as a scheme. Still, a 21% bad-throw rate is the passer's own doing, and it's new.

The slide is real, though partly explained by the schedule. His first two games came against defenses now ranked 19th and 24th and went fine, including a 15.9 CPOE at Tennessee. Then came Chicago, the Rams and Jacksonville, defenses now ranked 12th, 4th and 3rd. He went 0-3 in those games with -0.199 EPA per dropback and a -9.9 CPOE. The Rams game (12-of-27, 36% bad throws) was the low point. Jacksonville blitzed him into a 2.53-second release and a 6.1-yard average intended air depth.

The bigger story is now availability. Tanner McKee started Weeks 6 and 8, Hurts's practice report lists him as Out with no participation, and the depth chart has him as QB4 as of November 3, even though the site lists him Active. The dossier also credits him with a Week 7 start that isn't in the game log, so these numbers stop at Week 5. Until he is clearly back atop the depth chart, any outlook for him comes with that caveat.

strengths.title: Intermediate and deep throws still produce
strengths.body: On 46 attempts of 10+ air yards he is +0.878 EPA a play with an 8.7 CPOE, and the 10-19 band alone has added 26.7 EPA. This is the accurate intermediate passer from his 2022-2024 peak, so it's a skill with a long track record rather than a hot streak, though 46 attempts is a modest sample. Throwing deeper more often is the clearest path back to average-or-better efficiency.

strengths.title: Red-zone finishing and scramble value
strengths.body: He has five TDs on 14 red-zone attempts with a 14.8 CPOE, and his 12 scrambles average +0.33 EPA with five first downs. His TD rate ranks 15th even though his efficiency ranks 30th, which fits a career of converting near the goal line. The red-zone rate on 14 throws will cool, but the scramble value is a durable part of who he is.

strengths.title: Ball security on the ground
strengths.body: He has zero fumbles lost (1st of 47) and only a 1.9% interception rate. The turnover-worthy count still shows three fumbles, so this is partly luck that may not fully hold.

concerns.title: Accuracy collapse on short throws
concerns.body: His bad-throw rate of 21.4% is 7.1 points above last year and far outside his career norms. Short passes carry a -6.2 CPOE, and under-10 throws add up to -38 EPA. Some of this comes from a broken scheme and a 30th-ranked offense, but misses are on the quarterback. With no injury cause listed, it can't be dismissed as noise either.

concerns.title: His starting job is in question
concerns.body: McKee started two of the last three weeks, Hurts is listed Out and not practicing on his practice report, and he's QB4 on the depth chart. Whatever the reason, his weekly value now depends first on whether he plays at all.

concerns.title: Designed runs have stopped working
concerns.body: The designed-run game that once defined him is at 1.11 yards a carry and -0.339 EPA, with a stuff rate over 50%. Combined with rushing yards that have fallen every season since 2021, the floor his legs used to provide is thinner.

trend.note: He was solid in Weeks 1-2 against weaker defenses, then dropped to -0.199 EPA per dropback and a -9.9 CPOE in an 0-3 stretch against three top-12 defenses. McKee has since started twice.

nextGame.headline: Weak Giants rush meets missing receivers and an uncertain job
nextGame.body:
If Hurts starts, the Giants are a mixed matchup. They barely pressure the quarterback (31st in hit rate, 30th in sack rate), which matters for a passer who holds the ball 3.04 seconds. They also give quarterbacks touchdowns (2.43 a game, 28th). But they shut down what is working for him: they allow -0.292 EPA on deep throws (3rd), rank 8th against explosive passes, and allow the 3rd-fewest passing yards to quarterbacks. They also hold top tight ends well under their averages. That pushes him back toward the short game, where he's been at his worst.

Availability dominates. Hurts is QB4 on the depth chart and not practicing, so the first question is whether he plays. Both DeVonta Smith and Dontayvion Wicks are listed Out. Wicks has been his most productive target by far, so that loss stings badly, and Smith, his co-leader in targets, is out too. Lead back Dameon Pierce is on IR. On the Giants' side, LB Tremaine Edmunds is on IR, and S Jevon Holland and CB Greg Newsome are questionable with concussions. Losing those starters would soften the coverage and the middle of the field, where he has his best direction split. The Book makes Philadelphia a 3.5-point home underdog with a 40.5 total.

keyMatchups.title: His deep game vs stingy deep coverage
keyMatchups.body: His 10+ yard throws are the engine of his season, and New York ranks 3rd against deep passes. If Holland can't go, that gap narrows. Without that, he's left with his short game.

keyMatchups.title: Weak pass rush vs long holds
keyMatchups.body: The Giants' 30th-ranked sack rate gives him time to extend plays and scramble. Clean pockets are where his accuracy has a chance to recover.

keyMatchups.title: Receiver room without Wicks, Smith
keyMatchups.body: Wicks has added 19.9 EPA on 27 targets, and he's out along with Smith. Darius Cooper's efficient small sample and Dallas Goedert are what's left, and Goedert faces a defense that holds top tight ends 3.4 points under their norm.

nextGame.watch: Whether Hurts or McKee takes the first-team reps this week, and whether Smith and Wicks are cleared by Sunday.

restOfSeason.body:
If Hurts reclaims the job, expect a below-average passer with a usable fantasy floor from TDs and scrambles rather than a return to his 2022-2024 form. The intermediate accuracy is real and should keep producing. The red-zone TD rate and zero fumbles lost should drift back toward normal, and the short-game misses need a cause beyond the schedule before you assume they fix themselves. A softer run of defenses than the Week 3-5 stretch would help, as would getting Smith and Wicks back. Projected ranges: roughly 170-215 passing yards, 1.0-1.7 passing TDs and 15-28 rushing yards a game, about 12-18 PPR points when he starts.

If McKee keeps the job, none of this applies. The depth chart and practice reports are the first thing to check each week.
swingFactors: Whether he is the starter at all
Bad-throw rate on short passes normalizing

confidence.note: Job status unclear, game log stops at Week 5, and his top two receivers are out.
